summary: The stash CLI now embeds, at build time, the workspace versions of six sibling packages (stash, @cipherstash/stack, -drizzle, -supabase, prisma-next, wizard) and pins every install it runs or recommends (init installs, missing-package hints, context.json installCommand, native-module hint, wizard npx spawn) to those exact versions. Init also adds a version-skew check that warns on any installed version that differs from the embedded one and, interactively, offers (default yes) to reinstall the embedded version. The change fixes a real dist-tag problem and is well unit- and E2E-tested (CI green). The residual risk is release-mechanical: the repo's Changesets config does not version these packages together and stash has no runtime dependency on the adapters or wizard, so a published stash pins whatever sibling versions sat in the workspace at its build. Two consequences reviewers should weigh: (1) after a sibling ships without a stash bump, init treats the newer sibling as 'skew' and offers to downgrade it, and the stash-cli skill tells agents to align; (2) if a pinned sibling version is not actually on the registry (partial publish), every pinned install and the wizard spawn fail where a bare install used to succeed, and only a new release fixes it. Neither is shown to occur; both are plausible. Overall impact medium; focused review recommended.

behaviour_changes.description: tsup reads the version field of six sibling workspace manifests listed in RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS and embeds them as __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__ in both bundles; a missing or versionless manifest fails the build.
stash init installs @cipherstash/stack, the integration adapter and stash as exact-version specs (pkg@X) instead of bare names; source-mode runs with no embed fall back to bare names.

New skew check: any already-installed release-train package whose on-disk version string differs from the embedded version (older OR newer) is warned about; interactively init offers, with initialValue true, to reinstall the embedded version; non-interactively it only prints align commands.

Printed/recorded guidance is pinned: missing-package hint, requireStack hint, .cipherstash/context.json installCommand, install-eql manual note, native-binary recovery hint (was stash@latest), and stash wizard now runs npx @cipherstash/wizard@<embedded version>.
A present but malformed embed throws at module load of runtime-versions.ts, which is imported by the CLI entry, so a defective build would fail every command rather than silently unpinning.

Shipped agent skills (stash-cli, stash-drizzle, stash-dynamodb, stash-encryption, stash-supabase) now describe pinning; stash-cli tells agents to treat the skew warning as a real problem and align versions before continuing.

failure_scenarios.title: Stale pin after a sibling-only release makes init offer to downgrade a newer @cipherstash/* package
failure_scenarios.trigger: A release publishes a newer @cipherstash/stack or adapter (e.g. a fix) without a changeset for stash; a user who has that newer version installed then runs stash init with the latest stash.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Packages are not versioned together (.changeset/config.json fixed: [] and linked: []), and stash declares @cipherstash/stack only as a devDependency/optional peer with no dependency on the adapters or wizard, so a sibling bump does not necessarily republish stash. The published stash keeps the versions embedded at its own build. versionSkew() compares strings with !==, so a NEWER installed version is reported as skew; interactively the align is folded into a confirm with initialValue: true and installs pkg@<older embedded version>. The stash-cli skill tells agents to 'treat that warning as a real problem and align versions'.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Users or agents downgrade the encryption client or adapter to an older release, potentially reverting a fix (including a security fix) and changing package.json/lockfile, while the CLI frames the newer version as the problem. New installs also never receive the newer sibling until stash itself is re-released.

existing_verification.description: install-deps.test.ts covers skew where the installed version is OLDER (0.19.0) than expected; no case for a newer installed version.

missing_verification: A test (and a decision) for an installed version newer than the embedded one.
A release-process check that every release of a train package also re-releases stash, or that the pin set is refreshed.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Only warn/offer alignment when the installed version is lower (semver compare) or on a different major/prerelease line; never default-confirm a downgrade. Alternatively add the train packages to a Changesets fixed/linked group, or enforce that stash is bumped whenever a train package is. Soften the stash-cli skill wording for newer-version skew.

failure_scenarios.title: Pinned sibling version not on the registry breaks init installs and stash wizard for every new user
failure_scenarios.trigger: During changeset publish, stash publishes but a sibling's publish fails or is skipped (publishes are per-package), or a sibling's workspace version is otherwise never published.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The embed is taken from workspace manifests at build time (pnpm run build && changeset publish), not from what the registry accepted. The installs and the wizard runner now request pkg@<exact version>; npm/pnpm fail with ETARGET/404 if that version does not exist. Previously the bare name always resolved to something.
failure_scenarios.consequence: stash init fails to install dependencies (step reports still-missing packages) and stash wizard fails to launch for all users of that stash version; because npm publishes are irreversible, recovery requires publishing the missing sibling or a new stash release. Failure is loud, not silent.
